newsitem.title: UK: Survey shows Britons still worried about beef.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows Britons still worried about beef.

text.p: British people are still worried about the safety of eating beef and want the government to do more to reassure them about the risks of mad cow disease, a survey released on Friday has found.

The NOP poll found 70 percent of those surveyed still felt worried, one year after government scientists said they had identified a new variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), the human version of mad cow disease.
They said the variant probably came from eating beef infected with bovine spongiform enchephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease).
"Some 73 percent of women felt that the government should do more to reassure people about British beef compared with 68 percent of men," NOP said in a statement.
The government insists British beef is safe to eat because of rules that require slaughterhouses to remove potentially infectious material.
But the Agriculture Ministry has also admitted slaughterhouses have been caught breaking the rules in the past and is currently fighting off criticism about hygiene in abattoirs.
Poor hygiene can lead to outbreaks of food poisoning, such as the E coli bacteria that killed 18 elderly people in Scotland this year and last.
